questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The University of Copenhagen and Queen Mary University of London were both very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A Queen Mary counsellor helped me adding and dropping classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The staff is really trying to help but unfortunately they gave us wrong information quite a few times. We did not know all of our exam dates before two weeks before the exam. Moreover, we were told that all exams would be done by December 16th which is incorrect because we also have exams in January.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed with family.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is quite expensive in London.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You make an application to get KU's nomination which is quite easy and fast. After getting the nomination you must apply for Queen Mary University which is also quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both Queen Mary and KU are very helpful if you have any questions. The Queen Mary staff replies very fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: You cannot count on the module description on the website of Queen Mary. They will send you a separate document with the modules you are allowed to take. I was told that I could take classes from level 4, 5 and 6 but that is not true. You get to choose between 10 classes and most of them are about philosophy and how philosophers look at law and justice.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to London if you want to experience the city. I can recommend doing family law and competition law.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It felt like they gave exchange students the new classes which they weren't sure about if they were good enough for their normal students. Moreover, they do not know our exams dates which they should have told us from the beginning. I have exams while traveling in January because they told us that we would be done before December 16th. This will also affect the Erasmus grant where my end date should have been in January.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The classes are very boring and the teachers are having 2 hours monologues where they ask max. 2 questions. Most teachers do not give us breaks and if they do we get 2 min so we can't even make it to the toilets. The tutorials are good because we actually get to participate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They do not include students very much and no breaks. The teacher will talk nonstop for 2 hours. They have very low expectations to the students. They have seminars, lectures and tutorials. I did like the tutorials a lot because students are involved. The tutorials are quite similar to the way they teach at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Family law, competition law, climate justice anf democracy and justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Family law and competition law because you learn something in those classes and they are quite interesting. You also meet British students in these classes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I lived with family so my rent was very low compared to other places in London.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I spent a lot more on food than expected. Also alcohol is more expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many societies that I can't even say a society that is not created.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It is good to join a society of any kind if you want to meet British students. Your classes will mainly consist of exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out to eat. Covent Garden is really nice. If you want to go out, I liked Soho the most. Shoreditch is also good if you want to go to a bar. Many parts of the Tube closes at night so download the Uber app so you can get home.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is not that different from Denmark so it was not that difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a society.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: British people are very open and talk a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do not go for the academics but for the experience, save up some money prior to the exchange because it is very expensive, join a society if you want to talk to British students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are exams in January so do not plan on working full time in this period. The exams can be turned in online so you do not have to be present but you will have to spend some time at home writing the exams. All the exams have been essays.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My English has improved a lot and I met a lot of people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Staying motivated for classes. Not many students participates in the classes and the teacher rarely asks questions to engage the students except for the tutorials.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
